what_changed.text: Status escalated to Crisis Acceleration — Transition. Tier 2 confirming score reached 6/20, crossing the combined T1+T2 gate.
Gold at $5,069 with YoY at +72% and 8-week momentum at +9.8%. Both Gold Momentum and Treasury Divergence at maximum.
Commodity/Gold ratio collapsed 25% YoY — scoring at 1. Gold repricing against everything, not an inflation trade.
Oil/SPR Capacity Ratio at score 2. Oil at $96 with SPR at 415M barrels — refill capacity severely constrained at current prices.

contrarian: Wall Street is framing gold’s run as an inflation trade. The Canary says otherwise. If this were inflation, commodities would be running with gold — copper, oil, and the GSCI would be surging. Instead, the commodity/gold ratio has collapsed 25%. Gold is repricing against everything: stocks, bonds, and commodities alike.

This is a monetary confidence signal. Gold is telling you something about the monetary system itself, not about CPI prints. Gold has posted +72% YoY while Treasury yields stayed flat — the last time a divergence this extreme appeared was the early 1970s, after Nixon closed the gold window but before the market fully processed the implications.

Meanwhile, the Fed is quietly expanding its balance sheet through $40B/month in short-duration purchases while publicly maintaining a tightening stance. The Canary sees through the narrative to the mechanism: the balance sheet is growing, and the purchases are only “short duration” for now. New supply-chain indicators add another layer: copper smelters are paying miners to take concentrate (TC/RCs at $0), and the silver market is running its 5th consecutive annual deficit with 800 million ounces of cumulative shortfall. Meanwhile, crude oil is at $96 while the SPR sits at 58% capacity — refill capacity is severely constrained at current prices.

divergence.description: The single most predictive indicator in The Canary. When gold surges and yields don’t follow, the bond market is being artificially suppressed — either through direct purchases or implicit policy. This divergence preceded every major regime transition in the last 50 years.
divergence.current_reading: Current reading: Gold +72% YoY while 10Y yields are flat. The gold-colored area shows the divergence at its widest point in modern history — gold has nearly doubled in a year while the bond market hasn’t moved. Historically, this gap closes violently: either yields spike to catch up (bad for bonds), or gold is proven right about debasement (bad for the monetary system). At this magnitude, the divergence has moved beyond “tension” into “stealth suppression.”

positioning.intro: Crisis Acceleration — Transition is the phase where signals compound. The Canary has crossed the combined T1+T2 gate. Historically, the largest gains in gold, Bitcoin, and hard assets occur during this transition — not after crisis is fully confirmed. The short-term Treasury buffer remains for now as a liquidity parking lot, but gets eliminated if the framework reaches full Crisis Acceleration — the point where Treasuries themselves become the problem.

posture.label: Gold — overweight
posture.reason: Gold Momentum + Divergence both at 2 simultaneously. This signal cluster has preceded every major regime transition. At +72% YoY, momentum has already exceeded the Score 2 threshold.

posture.label: Bitcoin — overweight
posture.reason: Functions as high-beta gold in monetary regime transitions. Dropped 57% in 2020 acute crisis, then 18x’d. Position size for volatility.

posture.label: Short-term Treasuries — hold
posture.reason: T-bills under 1-year maturity. Reduces portfolio volatility and provides dry powder to deploy during drawdowns. Eliminated at Crisis Acceleration when Treasuries themselves become the problem.

posture.label: Critical materials — overweight
posture.reason: Copper TC/RCs scoring at 2 (smelters paying miners). Physical premium at 4% — below the 5% trigger but elevated. If China escalates export controls, conviction increases.

posture.label: Equities — underweight
posture.reason: S&P/Gold ratio at 1.34 and falling — equities losing purchasing power in real terms. Full elimination at Crisis Acceleration.

posture.label: Long Treasuries — underweight
posture.reason: The Gold/Treasury Divergence says yields are artificially suppressed. The T-bill buffer gives short-duration exposure; long duration carries asymmetric downside when the divergence closes.

escalation: Fed shifts to long-duration purchases while The Canary reads Early Warning or above → immediate Crisis Acceleration (Override Rule #4). QE launched from Stable does not trigger — it’s a crisis response, not a cause. Explicit YCC (stated yield target) triggers unconditionally.
Treasury auction B/C drops below 2.0 → demand crisis signal. Currently masked by Fed purchases — watch what happens if they pause.
Tier 2 confirming score reaches ≥6 (currently 6/20) → triggers Transition via combined T1+T2 gate. Watch copper premiums, China controls, and Fed deferred asset for movement.
Gold 8-week momentum breaks +15% → acceleration signal. Currently at +9.8% — below the threshold.
deescalation: Gold YoY drops below +30% while yields rise → genuine tightening. Divergence closes from the gold side.
Fed resumes QT at full pace → balance sheet contracting. Not just slowing purchases — actively shrinking.
Tier 1 drops to 0–2 (currently 5/10) → returns to Stable. Would require gold momentum AND divergence to normalize.
Deficit/GDP falls below 5% → structural fiscal pressure easing. Currently at ?% and rising.

track_record.intro: Applied retroactively across nine historical periods, The Canary identified every major regime transition 3–6 months early with near-zero false positives.

adversarial.label: Gold rally (+25%)
adversarial.result: No signal ✔ — cyclical bounce with no yield divergence or Fed expansion. Gold reversed within a year.

adversarial.label: Gold bear market (−45%)
adversarial.result: No false signal ✔ — real tightening with rising yields. The system correctly read this as non-monetary.

adversarial.label: Fed tightening cycle
adversarial.result: No false signal ✔ — QT was running and balance sheet shrinking. No divergence to trigger on.

adversarial.label: LTCM / Russia crisis
adversarial.result: Correctly filtered ✔ — financial stress but no monetary regime implications. Fed cut rates and markets stabilized.

adversarial.label: SVB banking stress
adversarial.result: Brief signal, self-corrected ✔ — initial spike in Fed lending resolved within weeks. No sustained monetary shift.

adversarial.label: 30-year balance sheet expansion
adversarial.result: Right on direction, open on timing — BOJ’s experiment is still running. The framework flags the trajectory correctly but can’t call the endpoint.
